neighbours.label: the heart as a pump: its chambers and pumping capacity (ventricles, ability to pump), as against rhythm, which the + pole takes
fire: A damaged valve can seriously limit the heart's ability to move blood around the body.
On the scan, the left ventricle appeared much larger than the right ventricle in this man.
Doctors fitted a right ventricular assist device while she waited for a transplant.
Regular training may strengthen your heart's ability to pump during hard effort.
Her enlarged heart could no longer pump enough blood to meet the demands of the body.
In dilated cardiomyopathy, the ventricle is stretched and contracts only weakly.
Fluid backs up when the failing heart cannot empty its chambers with each beat.
The surgeon measured how much blood the left ventricle ejects with every contraction.
quiet: A damaged nerve can seriously limit the arm's ability to move around the shoulder.
On the scan, the left kidney appeared much larger than the right kidney in this man.
Doctors fitted a cochlear implant while she waited for a place at the clinic.
Regular training may strengthen your lungs' capacity to breathe during hard effort.
Her irregular heartbeat could suddenly race and leave her dizzy and short of breath.
In atrial fibrillation, the rhythm is erratic and the pulse feels fluttery.
Bile backs up when the blocked liver cannot empty its ducts after each meal.
The surgeon measured how much urine the left kidney drains during every hour.

notes: The + pole fires around arrhythmia and promotes ' arr', ' rhythm'; the - pole looks like the mechanical side of the same domain. Near misses are rhythm sentences and other organs.
